title: Candidate Welcome Lab — WeekZero setup & access runbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, operational runbook to remove friction in the first 72 hours (WeekZero) for new hires. It bundles pre-boarding access steps, manager/buddy orchestration, a lightweight interview-rubric primer for any concurrent hiring activity, and a short conviction log for hiring/enablement signals.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: hiring managers, people ops coordinators, IT onboarding, hiring interviewers, hiring committee leads, buddy engineers.
- Scope: full-stack for WeekZero (72 hours) to Day10 activation. Not a replacement for the full 30/90 plan but a practical checklist to avoid common stalls (credentials, access, first day expectations).

Quick notes to self (people ops):
- Keep this doc intentionally prescriptive and minimal — managers want checkboxes.
- Reuse/access templates from Confluence ONBOARD-7234.
- Add region-specific KMS access steps later (APAC differences).

PRE-START (3–7 days before start) — People Ops / Recruiter
- Confirm candidate accepted offer and timezone.
- Send welcome email with: day1 agenda, calendar invites for orientation, Slack invite, and an ask: personal bio + 2 things to share in intro.
- Create role folder in Google Drive and pre-populate with: role doc, first-week sprint, tech stack cheat-sheet.
- Kick off IT: ticket HR-IT-ACCESS with required apps list (GitHub, GCP/AWS Console access, Slack, Okta app entitlements). Include manager-approved least-privilege list.
- Request hardware provisioning: laptop spec and peripherals, shipping address, estimated delivery.
- Get security checklist started: NDA/KBA checks + SSO provisioning.
- Add candidate to payroll/benefits pipeline (people ops).

DAY 0 (end of day before start) — IT / People Ops
- Confirm laptop serial and tracking link to new hire and manager.
- Pre-stage a temporary local admin account if remote imaging will take >2 hours first day.
- Provision Okta invite and confirm MFA options are communicated.
- Share internal maps: org chart (compact), Slack etiquette doc, and passphrase about first 24 hours.

DAY 1 — Manager checklist (morning)
- 09:00 — Welcome call (15–20m): quick intros, expectations, first week focus.
- 09:30 — Team intro + buddy pairing announcement in Slack channel #team-<pod>.
- 10:00 — Workspace tour (virtual): primary repos, infra dashboard links, where to find runbooks.
- 11:00 — Tech access validation: confirm Okta, GitHub, internal VPN, and one sample repo clone. Manager hands off to buddy for pairing.
- Day1 deliverable: create a single PR that updates a docs/README (low-risk, high-feedback first task).

DAY 1 — Buddy (first 24 hours)
- Run through local dev setup checklist (5–6 steps).
- Shadow pairing: small code edit + run tests.
- Point to 3 very small tickets labeled "good first task".
- Schedule 30m recurring check-ins for first two weeks (every other day then weekly).

IT & SECURITY — Access quick checks (highest friction items)
- Okta: confirm app entitlements + add to groups for role-based infra.
- GitHub: ensure team membership, repo access, and deploy key access if applicable.
- Cloud console: least-privilege role, test find-of a dedicated staging resource.
- Vault/KMS: ensure dev-level secret read for non-prod buckets.
- Internal VPN / Bastion: test SSH tunnel to staging host.
- If anything fails, tag ticket HR-IT-ACCESS with severity P0 and escalate to SRE oncall.

FIRST 72 HOURS — To reduce cognitive load
- Limit meeting invites to the absolute minimum: orientation, 1:1 with manager, buddy pairing, benefits/HR drop-in.
- Focus deliverable: commit a docs change + a test-run on local dev.
- Have manager send an explicit "You are allowed to ask for help" message — reduces ramp anxiety.

DAY 3 — Manager follow-up
- Review Day1 deliverable; give written feedback.
- Confirm access to all remaining tools.
- Agree on 10-day activation sprint deliverables and acceptance criteria.

10-DAY ACTIVATION SPRINT (example lightweight scope)
- Goal: reach a low-confidence feature ownership on a narrow area (e.g., implement tracing for a small endpoint, add a small metric, or complete a user-facing doc).
- Acceptance criteria (examples): code merged to staging, unit tests passing, short doc published.
- Delivery checkpoints: Day3 review, Day7 demo sync (10–15m), Day10 ship.

INTERVIEW RUBRIC PRIMER (for concurrent hiring panels)
- Use this only when new hire is in loop or manager still interviewing. Aim for consistent signals.
- Scale: 1 (red flag) — 2 (needs training) — 3 (meets) — 4 (outstanding).
- Dimensions (minimal set):
  * Problem decomposition (clarity + tradeoffs)
  * Coding fluency (idiomatic code, correctness)
  * Systems reasoning (scaling, latency, failure modes)
  * Ownership instincts (past examples, cross-team influence)
  * Communication & collaboration (explains clearly, listens)
- Quick guidance for interviewers: write 1–2 sentence evidence for each score. If any dimension = 1, candidate needs follow-up.

EXAMPLE RUBRIC SNIPPET (one row as stringable note)
- Candidate: "X" | Problem decomposition: 3 (structured approach, clarified constraints) | Coding: 2 (minor syntax gaps) | Systems: 3 | Ownership: 4 | Comm: 3 | Notes: good ownership examples from past role; needs practice on code style.

CANDIDATE DEBRIEF TEMPLATE (post-interview, used in hiring sync)
- Quick summary (1–2 lines):
- Strong signals: (bulleted)
- Concerns / risks: (bulleted)
- Recommended next step: [no-hire / take-home / follow-up call / hire] + rationale
- On a scale of 1–10, hiring manager conviction: __

CONVICTION LOG (live during first 10 days)
- Purpose: capture evolving confidence in hire and operational blockers.
- Example entries (format: date | actor | observation | impact | action):
  2025-02-12 | buddy | Could not access staging DB until 14:00 | blocked Day1 local test | IT ticket created HR-IT-ACCESS-49, resolved by 15:30
  2025-02-14 | manager | Delivered small doc PR and tests | early positive signal | bumped confidence to 7/10

REGULAR CHECKPOINTS (who owns)
- Day3: manager (written feedback)
- Day7: buddy (hands-on demo)
- Day10: manager + eng lead (light post-mortem on ramp blockers)

KNOWN RISKS AND MITIGATIONS
- Hardware delay: provide loaner image and temporary admin to unblock first day.
- Access gating (SSO/entitlements): pre-sign SSO invite and validate group mapping in Okta before start.
- Over-meeting: manager to block focus hours Day1–3.

TEMPLATE CHECKLIST (copyable)
- [ ] Offer accepted + benefits pipeline kicked
- [ ] Welcome email sent with Day1 agenda
- [ ] Hardware shipping confirmed
- [ ] Okta invite pending
- [ ] GitHub access provisioned
- [ ] Cloud console IAM role assigned for staging
- [ ] Buddy assigned and calendar invite sent
- [ ] Day1 PR task created and labeled "first-touch"
- [ ] 30m recurring check-ins scheduled for 2 weeks
- [ ] Conviction log created in hire folder

DOCS & LINKS (placeholders)
- Onboarding master checklist: confluence/ONBOARD-7234
- IT ticket queue: JIRA/HR-IT-ACCESS
- New joiner Slack channel template: slack:#new-joiners-template

OPEN QUESTIONS / TODO (people ops)
- Add region-specific KMS access steps for EMEA and APAC — Leah to lead.
- Decide whether to automate dev key provisioning for contractors — follow-up with Security.
- Build a simple dashboard (sheet) to track first-week blockers (columns: hire, start date, blocker, owner, resolved_at).

END NOTES
- This doc is intentionally concise; drop additional checklists back into the role folder as they are needed.
- If you hit repeated patterns where new hires are blocked >6 hours, escalate to SRE/infra for a retro.

VERSION HISTORY
- 2025-02-10 — draft created by Aisha Patel
- 2025-02-14 — added rubric primer and conviction log examples (Marco Ruiz)
- 2025-02-18 — refined IT escalation flow and Day1 deliverable guidance (Leah Zhang)

(Author: Aisha Patel — People Ops)
